title: 3rd Truth The Importance Of This Mystery And Reference To The Risale I Nur

questions.question: What is the main subject of this passage?
questions.answer: It explains a deep proof of Allah’s oneness and power, especially how the greatest things and the smallest things are equally easy for Him.

questions.question: How does the passage describe this truth in relation to Islam and faith?
questions.answer: It presents it as a major foundation of Islam and a very deep source of ایمان, showing its central importance.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does explaining this truth make possible for people to understand?
questions.answer: It helps people grasp a hidden mystery about how all created things come into being.

questions.question: What effect does this mystery have on philosophy, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It leaves philosophy unable to fully solve or master this issue by itself.

questions.question: To whom is repeated thanks and praise given in the passage?
questions.answer: They are given to the Merciful Creator.

questions.question: What role is attributed to the Risale-i Nur in this passage?
questions.answer: It is said to have explained, uncovered, and firmly proven this difficult and amazing mystery.

questions.question: How certain does the passage say these proofs are?
questions.answer: It says they are established with the kind of certainty people have about a basic mathematical fact.

questions.question: In what way does the passage support its claim about the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: It points to several specific sections in that work where this matter is argued in detail.

questions.question: Why does the passage not fully explain the whole subject here?
questions.answer: Because it leaves the full treatment to those earlier sections and only plans to give a brief outline here.

questions.question: What does the passage say the writer intended to present after this introduction?
questions.answer: The writer intended to mention the basic proofs and refer briefly to thirteen mysteries, like steps or a table of contents.

questions.question: How much of that plan had already been completed?
questions.answer: The first and second mysteries had already been written.

questions.question: Why was the rest left unfinished?
questions.answer: Two strong obstacles, one physical and one non-physical, caused the writer to stop.

questions.question: What comparison is used to express Allah’s ease in creating both huge and tiny things?
questions.answer: The passage says the largest universal reality and the smallest individual thing are no different for Allah in difficulty.

questions.question: Why is this truth described as a “mystery” or “riddle”?
questions.answer: Because it is a profound matter that human reasoning alone struggles to fully reach.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest the Qur’an does with this mystery?
questions.answer: It says the Qur’an opens up and explains it like unlocking something hidden.

questions.question: What does the passage imply about ordinary human philosophy compared with revelation-based explanation?
questions.answer: It suggests philosophy falls short, while the revealed explanation successfully uncovers the issue.

questions.question: What feeling is shown after mentioning this truth and its explanation?
questions.answer: Strong gratitude and praise to Allah are shown.

questions.question: Why is the Risale-i Nur praised in this passage?
questions.answer: Because it is presented as a means through which this difficult issue was clarified and proven.

questions.question: What kind of arguments are said to support that explanation?
questions.answer: Firm and decisive arguments are said to support it.

questions.question: Does the passage claim this matter is only mentioned briefly elsewhere, or carefully proven in several places?
questions.answer: It says it is carefully proven in several places.

questions.question: Why does the passage refer readers to other sections of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: Because those sections already give the fuller explanation, so this passage only needs to lay out the foundations briefly.

questions.question: What picture does the passage give by comparing the mysteries to steps or contents?
questions.answer: It gives the sense of an organized path of learning, where each part helps a person move deeper into understanding.

questions.question: What can we infer about the writer’s condition from the mention of two obstacles?
questions.answer: We can infer that the writer wanted to continue but was prevented by serious difficulties.

questions.question: What balance does the passage keep between confidence and limitation?
questions.answer: It shows confidence that the truth has been proven, while also admitting that the present discussion remains incomplete.

questions.question: What key belief is being defended in this passage?
questions.answer: The passage defends tawhid, the oneness of Allah, together with the perfection of His power.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the importance of this belief for Muslim life and understanding?
questions.answer: It describes it as one of the most important supports of Islam and faith.

questions.question: What is the special point about Allah’s power that the passage highlights?
questions.answer: It highlights that for Allah there is no meaningful difference between creating something vast and creating something tiny.

questions.question: What is said to be uncovered by explaining this truth?
questions.answer: A hidden secret about the creation of beings is said to be brought to light.

questions.question: According to the passage, what happens to philosophy when facing this secret?
questions.answer: Philosophy is shown to be powerless to solve it on its own.

questions.question: How does the passage show that its claim is not meant to be unsupported?
questions.answer: It refers to specific writings where detailed and convincing proofs have already been given.

questions.question: What kind of teaching method is used in this passage after mentioning those detailed writings?
questions.answer: It uses a summary method, giving the foundations first instead of repeating the full proofs.

questions.question: What structure was the writer planning for the summary?
questions.answer: The writer planned a list of thirteen mysteries, presented like stages in a lesson.

questions.question: How many of those stages were completed according to the passage?
questions.answer: Only the first two were completed.

questions.question: What prevented the project from being finished?
questions.answer: Strong outward and inward obstacles prevented the rest from being written.

questions.question: What central claim about creation is introduced at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: The passage introduces the claim that Allah creates the greatest and the smallest with equal ease.

questions.question: Besides being a proof, how else is this truth described?
questions.answer: It is described as beneficial wisdom, a great key, a difficult puzzle, and a major basis of faith.

questions.question: What does the passage say becomes opened or unlocked through presenting this truth?
questions.answer: It says a hidden key of the Qur’an is opened, making a secret of creation understandable.

questions.question: How is human intellectual effort alone portrayed here?
questions.answer: It is portrayed as limited and unable by itself to fully solve this deep matter.

questions.question: What does the passage say the Risale-i Nur accomplished?
questions.answer: It says that work solved, revealed, and established this profound issue.

questions.question: How strong are the proofs said to be in those writings?
questions.answer: They are described as conclusive and highly certain.

questions.question: What is the purpose of mentioning named sections from other works?
questions.answer: The purpose is to direct the reader to fuller discussions where the subject has already been carefully demonstrated.

questions.question: Why does the passage still continue after referring to those sections?
questions.answer: Because the writer still wants to provide a short presentation of the foundations and some hints about the larger structure.

questions.question: What does the image of “thirteen steps” help the reader understand?
questions.answer: It helps the reader see that the explanation was meant to unfold gradually and clearly, one part after another.

questions.question: What emotional tone appears in the statement that the writer had to stop?
questions.answer: There is a tone of regret, since the writer says the work was left unfinished because of strong barriers.

questions.question: What deep problem is this passage trying to answer?
questions.answer: It is trying to explain how Allah’s oneness and power mean that creating all things, big or small, is equally easy for Him.

questions.question: Why is this explanation important according to the passage?
questions.answer: Because it supports a core truth of Islam and strengthens the foundations of belief.

questions.question: What kind of secret about creation is mentioned?
questions.answer: The passage mentions a hidden and difficult secret about how beings are brought into existence.

questions.question: How is this secret related to the Qur’an?
questions.answer: The passage says the Qur’an contains the key that opens and explains it.

questions.question: What judgment does the passage make about philosophy in this area?
questions.answer: It says philosophy cannot overcome or fully answer this issue.

questions.question: How does the passage present the contribution of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: It presents it as a work that clarified and proved this secret in a strong way.

questions.question: What shows that the passage wants the reader to trust that claim?
questions.answer: It points to exact parts of the work where detailed evidence is said to be found.

questions.question: Why are those detailed parts not repeated fully in this passage?
questions.answer: Because the writer chooses to leave the full exposition there and only give a short outline here.

questions.question: What was the writer planning to include in this shorter outline?
questions.answer: The writer was planning to mention the roots of the proof and to point toward thirteen mysteries.

questions.question: What does the phrase about steps or contents suggest about the organization?
questions.answer: It suggests the subject was arranged carefully, almost like chapters in a lesson plan.

questions.question: How far did the writer get in carrying out that plan?
questions.answer: The writer completed only the first two parts.

questions.question: What reason is given for not continuing?
questions.answer: Serious material and spiritual-type obstacles stopped the work.

questions.question: What truth about Allah’s power is at the heart of this passage?
questions.answer: The heart of the passage is that Allah’s power handles the largest and smallest created things without any difference in difficulty.

questions.question: How is this truth connected to tawhid?
questions.answer: It serves as a proof of Allah’s absolute oneness, since such power belongs only to Him.

questions.question: What does the passage call this truth besides a proof?
questions.answer: It calls it a wisdom, a hidden key, a hard puzzle, and a major support of religion and faith.

questions.question: What result comes from setting out this truth clearly?
questions.answer: It allows a hidden matter about creation to be recognized and understood.

questions.question: How is philosophy described when faced with this matter?
questions.answer: It is described as unable to deal with it successfully.

questions.question: What response of the heart does the passage model after mentioning this explanation?
questions.answer: It models deep shukr and praise to Allah.

questions.question: What is said about the certainty of the proofs found in the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: They are said to be as certain as the clearest basic truths.

questions.question: How does the passage show that this is not only a personal opinion?
questions.answer: It supports the point by referring to multiple written discussions where the matter was demonstrated with evidence.

questions.question: What teaching choice does the writer make in this passage?
questions.answer: The writer chooses not to repeat all the full arguments but instead to summarize the basic foundations.

questions.question: What was meant by mentioning thirteen mysteries?
questions.answer: It meant that the full explanation was planned in thirteen connected parts.

questions.question: What had already been written from that plan?
questions.answer: The first and second mysteries had already been written down.

questions.question: What final detail explains why the rest is missing?
questions.answer: The writer says two major obstacles, one outward and one inward, forced the work to stop.
